plainTranslation: Affection and emotional need slightly at odds. What the Venus person offers isn't quite what the Moon person needs to feel cared for. Failure mode: a recurring sense of being loved in the wrong language. Learn the other's actual needs - workable and worth it.
policy: Governed by synastry-policy. Descriptive, not deterministic; intensity is never treated as obligation, safety concerns override astrology.
note: Imported from approved project marquee synastry aspect material. Source file was not copied into the repository.
summaryDeep:
The care is there, but the delivery can be off. You may both want to make each other feel loved, yet keep missing the mark. One person gives what they would want to receive, while the other is left thinking, "That is not really what I needed."

The good news is that there is usually genuine affection underneath the frustration. You likely want the best for each other. The challenge is that good intentions do not automatically create emotional connection. If you keep assuming the other person should just know what works, you can end up feeling disappointed even when both of you are trying.

Over time, these small misses can start to tell a bigger story. You may begin to think your needs are not important, while they may feel like nothing they do is ever enough. That is when a simple misunderstanding turns into resentment.

Be direct. Tell this person what helps you feel cared for. Ask them what matters to them too. Stop grading each other on mind-reading. This connection gets stronger when you focus less on how love should look and more on whether it is actually reaching the other person.
